section_1.title: The Flatland Limitation (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Define dimensions as degrees of freedom. Introduce the concept of a 'Flatlander'—a 2D square living on a plane. Explain that they can perceive length and width but cannot conceive of 'height' or depth.
section_1.example: A 2D ant crawling on a sheet of paper. If a 3D sphere passes through the paper, the ant only sees a circle that grows and shrinks, not a sphere.

section_2.title: Prerequisites: The Power of Projections (0:45-1:45)
section_2.content: Teach the concept of geometric projection. Explain that a 3D object's shadow on a 2D surface is a projection. Emphasize that different rotations of the same object result in different 2D silhouettes.
section_2.example: A wireframe cube shadow. As you rotate the 3D cube, the 2D shadow transforms from a square to a complex hexagon.

section_3.title: The Dimensional Shift Puzzle: The Tesseract (1:45-3:15)
section_3.content: Introduce the Tesseract (4D hypercube). Explain how we visualize 4D objects: by projecting them into 3D, just as we project 3D into 2D. Use the 'unfolding' technique where a 3D cube unfolds into a 2D cross, and a 4D cube unfolds into a 3D 'cross' of cubes.
section_3.example: Animation of a 3D cube unfolding into a 2D net, transitioning to an animation of a Tesseract unfolding into 8 cubes (the 'Dalí Cross').

section_4.title: Practical Logic: Solving Dimensional Puzzles (3:15-4:15)
section_4.content: Apply the shift logic to a concrete problem: How do you identify a hidden object given only its slices or projections? Focus on 'Cross-sectional reasoning'—reconstructing a 3D solid from a series of 2D slices.
section_4.example: A MRI scan concept: Seeing a 'series of shapes' (circles, triangles) and deducing it is a cone or a sphere.

section_5.title: Summary and Conceptual Leap (4:15-5:00)
section_5.content: Recap: To understand higher dimensions, we look for invariants (properties that stay the same) despite changes in projection. Challenge the student to visualize a 4D creature observing our 3D world.
section_5.example: Closing animation: A 3D character (a robotic bird) looking at its 2D shadow and realizing the shadow is only a partial truth of its existence.
